hypotheses.justification: The statement does not need it to elaborate: it only mentions `AlgebraTensorModule.map LinearMap.id f`. It is true without it, because `AdicCompletion I R` is flat over a Noetherian ring `R`. Mathlib already derives this as `flat_of_isNoetherian`, using `Module.Flat.iff_lTensor_injective'` with ideals `J`, which are finite modules. The general statement then follows from `Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap`, which needs no finiteness. Its conclusion is injectivity of `f.lTensor (AdicCompletion I R)`, which is the same function as `AlgebraTensorModule.map LinearMap.id f` (the coercion differs by `rfl` or a simp lemma). The proof changes: keep the current argument as a private finite-case lemma used only for ideal inclusions, prove flatness from it, and derive this lemma from flatness. The `[Module.Finite R M]` argument can be dropped by `omit ... in`. Since `M`, `N` live in `Type u`, the universe constraints of the flatness lemma are no obstacle. Deleting `[Module.Finite R N]` is equally possible via the same flatness route, and each can be removed on its own or both together.

The statement mentions neither finiteness of `N` nor anything that needs it. The result holds for arbitrary `R`-modules `M`, `N` once `R` is Noetherian, because `AdicCompletion I R` is flat over `R`. The proof goes through `Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap` applied to `f` with `Module.Flat R (AdicCompletion I R)`. To avoid circularity with `flat_of_isNoetherian`, which currently calls this lemma with `N = R` (finite because `R` is Noetherian), restructure the file: first a private finite-case lemma, then flatness, then this lemma. Deleting it is independent of deleting `[Module.Finite R M]`.
